explanation: Wednesday 2 September 1752 was followed by Thursday 14 September. Catholic countries had dropped only 10 days in 1582, but the old Julian calendar had slipped one more day since then.

claims.text: When Britain and its colonies adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1752, 11 days were dropped.
The 1752 British change dropped neither 10 nor 13 days.
In Britain, Wednesday 2 September 1752 was followed by Thursday 14 September 1752.
Catholic countries dropped 10 days when they adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1582.
By 1752 the Julian calendar was 11 days behind the Gregorian, one more than in 1582, because 1700 was a leap year only in the Julian calendar.
